text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > docs/CHATGPT_SIGN_IN.md <<'EOF'
# ChatGPT plan connection for Tacto

The analytical Astra agent can use the official **Sign in with ChatGPT** flow
for a locally hosted application. This is a separate authentication mode; it
does not convert API keys or API credits into a ChatGPT subscription.

The negotiation prompts, coefficients, package evaluation, models, SQLite
memory and final-action checks are unchanged by this connection. Both Astra
roles use the selected billing mode. Other legacy agents still use their
existing providers.

## Connect on this computer

```sh
uv sync
uv run tacto-chatgpt login
```

The command starts a temporary page on `127.0.0.1`. Click **Continue with
ChatGPT**, select your account/workspace and approve ChatGPT plan usage on
OpenAI's site. The local page displays the account when connected. It does not
start an Arena session. The connection window expires after 30 minutes; each
individual authorization attempt expires after 10 minutes.

Set this in the local `.env`:

```dotenv
OPENAI_AUTH_MODE=chatgpt
```

Then check access with one small streamed Astra request:

```sh
uv run tacto-chatgpt check
```

This checks the account's model catalog and requires `gpt-6-astra` exactly.
An unavailable model stops the operation; no other model is chosen. This check
uses ChatGPT plan allowance, but no Arena sessions. A successful check does not
reserve future allowance or guarantee future availability.

Existing analytical commands and run allowances stay the same. At construction,
the analytical router validates model access before the bounded practice runner
reserves a session. The runner records the authentication mode with experiment
metadata and the billing mode with each model call. Plan-access errors stop the
batch; there is no retry with a paid API key. These errors do not authorize a
Python-generated closing offer. Ksu's existing treatment of unrelated network
failures remains unchanged.

## Accounts and sign-out

```sh
uv run tacto-chatgpt status
uv run tacto-chatgpt models
uv run tacto-chatgpt select --profile <issued-client-id>
uv run tacto-chatgpt logout --profile <issued-client-id>
```

The sign-in page lists existing registrations and also allows another account.
Labels include a registration suffix, since the same email can belong to more
than one workspace. A router pins its selected registration for that run.
Signing out attempts remote revocation and clears the selected local tokens.
If revocation cannot be confirmed, disconnect the application in ChatGPT
Settings. Registration identifiers and this installation's host ID are retained
for later sign-in.

To deliberately return to API-key billing, set `OPENAI_AUTH_MODE=api_key`.
The existing `OPENAI_API_KEY` is retained and is never used as a fallback while
ChatGPT mode is selected. The example configuration keeps API-key mode as its
explicit default for other installations.

## Authentication boundary

- A dedicated `.chatgpt-auth/` directory in this checkout holds account records;
  it is ignored by Git, with directory mode `0700` and files `0600`.
- State, nonce and PKCE bind each callback to one pending attempt. Issuer,
  signature, audience, expiry and account identity are checked with PyJWT.
- The application discovers endpoints from OpenAI's official configuration and
  only accepts HTTPS endpoints on `auth.openai.com`.
- Renewable tokens are replaced atomically under a process lock. This first
  implementation targets macOS/Linux (`fcntl`).
- Credentials, authorization URLs and raw provider errors are not logged.
  Local account commands may display account labels and issued client IDs.
- Requests use the public Responses API with an OAuth bearer credential,
  `store=false`, `stream=true` and an array of input messages. The existing
  JSON schema, instructions and model are preserved. `max_output_tokens` is
  omitted because this route does not support it; elapsed-time and response-size
  limits remain. A terminal `response.completed` is required before parsing.
- The connection does not reuse Codex login files, browser cookies or an API key.

This integration does not compress prompts or improve negotiation strategy.
Large inputs still consume plan allowance. The local-app flow is not a blanket
permission to serve other people from a shared public deployment; confirm
OpenAI's hosted-app requirements before using it that way.

## Validation status

Source parsing, lint and dependency-lock checks passed. OpenAI discovery was
retrieved successfully and the local sign-in listener started. Browser automation
was blocked by its administrator-policy verification, so the user must complete
sign-in. Account/model access, token renewal, and inference are unverified until
that succeeds. No Arena session was started for this change, and no local
negotiation simulation was run.

## Official contract checked on 10 October 2026

- [Registration and sign-in](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/sign-in)
- [Accounts, refresh and revocation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/profiles-and-sessions)
- [Models and inference](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference)
- [Supported request fields](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/preview-limitations)
